findings.description: The user_data startup script embeds a literal AWS access key ID and secret access key (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) that are baked into instance metadata and baked into the AMI's cloud-init logs. Anyone able to read instance user-data (or the console/API) obtains these long-lived AWS credentials, which are not rotatable via the config and would allow persistent account access.

The ingress rule opens TCP port 22 (SSH) to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing remote administrative access to the internet. Combined with the subnet's map_public_ip_on_launch = true and the default route to the internet gateway, the EC2 host is directly reachable for brute-force and exploitation attempts from any source.

The EBS volume backing the portal server has no encrypted setting, so data written to the disk (including any OS, application, or credential material) is stored unencrypted. A snapshot or detached volume would then be readable by anyone with volume/snapshot access.

The bucket used as the VPC flow log destination has no server-side encryption configuration, so captured network metadata is stored unencrypted. Because flow logs contain source/destination IPs, ports, and traffic patterns, at-rest encryption is expected for this archive.
